result:
Done.

**Root cause:** `updateTerminal` (`variants/bug07/movegen.inc`) asked `moverInCheck` — which ignores its argument and tests the side that just *moved* — instead of `inCheckSide(sideToMove)`, so the mated king was never examined and every checkmate fell through to the stalemate branch.

**Files touched**
- `variants/bug07/movegen.inc` — the fix: `call moverInCheck` → `call inCheckSide` (one instruction; the assembled binary differs by exactly one byte)
- `variants/bug07/test_terminal.py` — new 7-case regression test
- `variants/bug07/Makefile` — runs it from `make test`
- `variants/bug07/chess.bin`, `chess.tap`, `pieces.inc` — rebuilt by `make`
- `FIX_NOTES.md`, `STATE.md` — at workspace root

**Gate status**
- Reported symptom reproduced before the fix, gone after — PASS (`Checkmate! White wins`, `black-mated`). All three bug-report mates and both stated controls behave as specified.
- `make test` (5 pre-existing checks) — PASS, ~25 s
- New test, standalone and in `make test` — PASS (7/7)
- Test proven two-sided by building mutants in `/tmp` (deleted): pre-fix build fails 4/6 with both controls passing; a naive "no moves ⇒ always mate" fails the stalemate control
- Review — 1 round, synchronous, **no defect in the fix**; gate closed (cap 3, used 1). The reviewer independently reproduced both mutants and ran 12 extra adversarial positions (promotion, double check, castling, en passant, smothered, 100th-halfmove mate, e.p.-pin stalemate, all three draw types) — all correct.

**Knowingly left open** — all six reviewer findings were `[OTHER]`, none a defect in the fix. I adopted one (a 7th case pinning that mate beats the 50-move claim, re-verified locally rather than taken on faith). The other five are pre-existing and out of scope, each recorded with its reason in `FIX_NOTES.md`: an already-terminal position loaded from tape or the editor is never adjudicated (`resetGameState` never calls `updateTerminal`); `aiMove`'s no-move path logs a phantom move; a stalemate that is also a 50-move/repetition position reports state 3 rather than 4 plus reason; take-back out of a finished game is unreachable by design; and the test runs the emulator twice per case with a fixed frame budget for the engine-mate case.
